title: Thinking Loop v4: compare resulting positions

D0.outcome: Explains why moves are compared by the positions they lead to, not by their first-move appeal.

D1.outcome: Given two or three resulting positions, ranks them and states the deciding feature of each (activity, structure, king safety, material).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses the better of two quiet continuations when the difference is a Silman-type imbalance rather than material.

D3.outcome: States which one feature decides the comparison and predicts how a one-feature change reverses it.

D4.outcome: In own games, the review shows a stated comparison of at least two resulting positions in critical positions, with prompts off.

misconceptions: The side with more material or more advanced pieces is better; counting settles it.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S2; docs/council-synthesis.md CD-3 (one versioned Thinking Loop)
docs/first-hours.md session 4 (threat check as loop v1)
conditions: Used when forcing lines have been exhausted and several quiet candidates remain.
A count of moves, pieces or space is only the first step; the check is what the extra moves were used for.
contrasts: A position that is ahead in force, space and time on the count but loses to one concrete idea.
Comparing resulting positions by material only while ignoring a king-safety difference.
Both continuations lead to the same position (a transposition).

soft_prereq_notes.POS.IMBALANCES.D1: supplies the vocabulary for the comparison
